_comment: text-decoration-thickness and text-underline-offset resolve their <length>, <percentage> and em forms against ONE reference: css-text-decor-4 §2.3 and §2.5 both make the percentage relative to 1em of the element's own font. With font-size: 20px that fixes 10% == 0.1em == 2px and 20% == 0.2em == 4px, which turns this file into a set of three-way EQUALITIES that a single platform can be held to on its own, without ever comparing it to another platform. That framing is deliberate. Neither property appears in fixtures/visual-test.json (only the `text-decoration` shorthand does), and the existing fixtures/properties/typography/text-decoration-thickness.json and text-underline-offset.json carry no `_text`, so the harness synthesizes a label from each COMPONENT NAME — different names, different string widths, different underline run lengths — which makes their rows mutually incomparable and leaves the em-versus-percentage question unasked. Here every component carries the identical `_text` and the identical box, font-size and decoration colour, so the declared value is the only thing that varies and cross-component byte comparison inside one platform is exact. The decoration colour is #e74c3c, distinct from the #111 text ink, so the underline band can be measured without separating it from glyph pixels. Cross-PLATFORM pairs in this file will diverge on font metrics (three different default families rasterise 'Hamburg 123' differently, the documented glyph wall); that is not the question this fixture asks. MUST MATCH within a platform: the three Thickness rows at 2px, and the three Offset rows at 4px. MUST DIFFER: Thickness_Px_2 vs Thickness_Px_6 and Offset_Px_4 vs Offset_Px_0 — the two rows that prove each property is read at all.

TDM_Thickness_Em_0_1._note: 0.1em against font-size 20px = 2px (css-text-decor-4 §2.3). EXPECTED: a 2px #e74c3c band under the text. Reference member of the thickness equality set.

TDM_Thickness_Percent_10._note: §2.3 resolves <percentage> against 1em, NOT against the auto thickness and NOT against the line box: 10% of 20px = 2px. EXPECTED byte-identical to TDM_Thickness_Em_0_1. A platform that resolves the percentage against anything else fails HERE ONLY, which separates percentage resolution from em resolution.

TDM_Thickness_Px_2._note: The absolute-length ground truth for the pair above: 2px. EXPECTED byte-identical to both. If this row alone is right, the property is applied but its relative units are not resolved.

TDM_Thickness_Px_6._note: PIN that the property is read at all. 6px must differ from TDM_Thickness_Px_2 by exactly 4 extra rows of #e74c3c across the underline's run. If the two are identical the platform is drawing its own auto thickness and ignoring the declaration — a silent drop that stays invisible to a three-way comparison if all three platforms do it.

TDM_Offset_Em_0_2._note: Thickness pinned at 2px so the only variable is the offset. 0.2em against font-size 20px = 4px below the font's own underline position (css-text-decor-4 §2.5). Reference member of the offset equality set.

TDM_Offset_Percent_20._note: §2.5 resolves this <percentage> against 1em as well: 20% of 20px = 4px. EXPECTED byte-identical to TDM_Offset_Em_0_2.

TDM_Offset_Px_4._note: Absolute-length ground truth for the offset pair: 4px. EXPECTED byte-identical to both rows above.

TDM_Offset_Px_0._note: PIN that the offset is read at all: 0px puts the band at the font's own underline position, exactly 4px above TDM_Offset_Px_4. Identical rows mean the declaration is being ignored. This is also the row that reveals whether the offset is measured from the font's underline position (spec) or from the alphabetic baseline, since only the former makes 0px a no-op.
